title: "G-PKI — Global, non-encapsulated PKI"
status: "Idealized Setup"

*G-PKI* (Global, non-encapsulated PKI) is part of *Idealized Setup and Resources* in the UC functionality encyclopedia. Status: an idealized setup assumption or shared resource.

A single, shared directory binding a verification key to the party that registered it, closing the gap [*F-Sig*](/uc/layer-3-public-key-primitives/f-sig/index.qmd) deliberately leaves open (its *Verify* takes a key unconnected to any caller, since keys are not assumed authenticated on their own). Global in Canetti's sense: at most one copy exists in any system, and every session reaches that one instance, since a second directory would mean a second notion of who owns which key.

## Functionality

State: a table $\mathtt{VK} : \mathcal{G}_{\mathsf{PKI}}.\mathbf{P} \to \mathcal{K} \cup \{\square\}$, initially everywhere $\square$.

- **Register(vk)**, from party $P$: an outsider (the adversary or the environment) acting for an *honest* $P$ only gets a peek at what's on file, never a write. Otherwise, if $P$ already has a key on file, that key is returned unchanged — the first successful call wins, permanently. Otherwise the offered key is sanitized to be fresh (not already claimed by another party) and recorded against $P$, then returned.
- **Retrieve(P)**: returns whatever is on file for $P$, or $\square$ if nobody has registered — answered to any caller, since a directory is public by nature.
- **Leak()**: returns the whole table, which is no more than *Retrieve* already gives out one entry at a time.

There is deliberately no *Deregister*: a key once bound stays bound. Revocation would be a genuine addition to this functionality, not a gap left open by oversight.

Below is the functionality itself, transcribed from [*UC for Gamers*](/surveys/uc-for-gamers/pdf/main.pdf#page=153) (§16.1, p. 152), line numbering and all. Reading it: $\mathsf{San}[\mathsf{Clean}](\cdot)$ resamples until the named predicate holds, with $\mathsf{Clean}_{\mathsf{reg}}$ written out at the end of the box; $\mathbf{C}$ is the set of corrupted parties; $A$ and $Z$ are the adversary's and environment's name components, so line 3 is the test that an outsider calling for an honest party gets a peek and not a write. The process id is pinned to a constant and $\mathbf{N}$ admits every standard, adversarial and environment id — that is what makes the directory *global*.

```{=html}
<div class="cj-interface">
<div class="cj-interface-head">
<div class="cj-interface-title">Functionality \(\mathcal{G}_{\mathsf{PKI}}\)</div>
<div class="cj-interface-params">\(\mathit{pid} := (\mathsf{GPKI},0,0)\), &nbsp; \(\mathbf{P}\), &nbsp; \(\mathbf{N} := \mathbf{Std} \cup \mathbf{A} \cup \mathbf{Z}\), &nbsp; \(\mathbf{U} := \emptyset\), &nbsp; \(\mathit{par} := \bot\)</div>
</div>
<div class="cj-interface-body">

<div class="cj-op">
<div class="cj-op-sig">Initialize():</div>
<ol class="cj-code" start="1">
<li>\(\mathtt{VK} : \mathcal{G}_{\mathsf{PKI}}.\mathbf{P} \to \mathcal{K} \cup \{\square\}\)</li>
<li>\(\mathtt{VK}[*] \gets \square\)</li>
</ol>
</div>

<div class="cj-op">
<div class="cj-op-sig"><span class="cj-id">id</span>.Register(<span class="cj-id">vk</span>)<span class="cj-op-from">from <span class="cj-id">id</span>′</span></div>
<ol class="cj-code" start="3">
<li>\(\textbf{if}\ \mathit{id}'.F \in \{A,Z\} \ \wedge\ \mathit{id}.P \notin \mathbf{C}\ \textbf{then}\)</li>
<li><span class="cj-ind">\(\textbf{return}\ \mathtt{VK}[\mathit{id}.P]\)</span><span class="cj-comment">// a peek, not a write</span></li>
<li>\(\textbf{if}\ \mathtt{VK}[\mathit{id}.P] \neq \square\ \textbf{then}\)</li>
<li><span class="cj-ind">\(\textbf{return}\ \mathtt{VK}[\mathit{id}.P]\)</span></li>
<li>\(\mathit{vk} \gets \mathsf{San}[\mathsf{Clean}_{\mathsf{reg}}](\mathit{vk}; \mathtt{VK})\)</li>
<li>\(\mathtt{VK}[\mathit{id}.P] \gets \mathit{vk}\)</li>
<li>\(\textbf{return}\ \mathit{vk}\)</li>
</ol>
</div>

<div class="cj-op">
<div class="cj-op-sig"><span class="cj-id">id</span>.Retrieve(<span class="cj-id">P</span>)<span class="cj-op-from">from <span class="cj-id">id</span>′</span></div>
<ol class="cj-code" start="10">
<li>\(\textbf{return}\ \mathtt{VK}[P]\)</li>
</ol>
</div>

<div class="cj-op">
<div class="cj-op-sig"><span class="cj-id">id</span>.Leak()<span class="cj-op-from">from <span class="cj-id">id</span>′</span></div>
<ol class="cj-code" start="11">
<li>\(\textbf{return}\ \mathtt{VK}\)</li>
</ol>
</div>

<div class="cj-op">
<div class="cj-op-sig">Clean<sub><span class="cj-rm">reg</span></sub>(<span class="cj-id">vk</span>; <span class="cj-rm">VK</span>):</div>
<ol class="cj-code" start="12">
<li>\(\textbf{return}\ \mathit{vk} \in \mathcal{K} \ \wedge\ \neg\exists\, P : \mathtt{VK}[P] = \mathit{vk}\)</li>
</ol>
</div>

</div>
</div>
```

## Known realizations

An idealization of a certificate authority or append-only public directory; realized in practice by any PKI whose issuance policy amounts to "first claim wins, no two parties share a key."

## Properties

Both proven with probability exactly $0$ against every occupant of the adversary slot:

- **Fixity.** A party's registered key never changes once set — every later registration by that party returns the same key, whatever is offered.
- **Binding.** No two distinct parties ever hold the same key on file.

Registering on behalf of a *corrupt* party proceeds freely (the adversary supplies whatever key it likes for a party it controls), so binding and fixity are guarantees about what the directory itself enforces, not about what an honest-looking key means.

## Formal artifacts

No machine-checked formalization yet.

*References:*

- Canetti, Shahaf, and Vald. [*Universally composable authentication and key-exchange with global PKI*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/432). In Public-Key Cryptography (PKC), Part II, volume 9615 of LNCS, pages 265–296, 2016.
- [*UC for Gamers*](/surveys/uc-for-gamers/index.qmd), this site's own book draft on composable security. Chapter "Public-Key Infrastructure" gives the functionality above and both properties in full.
